2.0.77._note: Captured on Factorio 2.0.77 from the release/2.0 recut at 0.2.1, which is the only place it can be taken: guest/go/data/engine.go keys on the RUNNING engine, so a 2.1 binary produces the 2.1 flavour whatever the manifest says. What this line pins that the 2.1.16 one cannot is the three things the version branch turns ON -- `not_colliding_with_itself` on bbb-linked-belt's collision mask, the `bbb-can-stack` marker prototype, and a mod-settings dump carrying the runtime-global `bbb-multi-edge-parts` beside the two startup cost settings, where the 2.1 arm carries the two alone. Per engine and per mod set: the dump carries every prototype every mod defined. Only the DEFAULT settings are hashed; the variant and speed arms assert values. RE-CAPTURED FOR 0.3.3's RECIPE CUSTOMIZER, and only `mod_settings_sha256` moved (196275f867f7f8b5 -> 258d44de08b43c9e, the same on both mod sets): `bbb-recipe-cost` gained the value `custom` and a `localised_description` composed from its six presets, and `bbb-recipe-ingredients` joined it as a third setting at order `aa`. Both `data_raw_sha256` values are unmoved and the normalised data-raw dumps were compared byte for byte either side of the change, which is what says the customizer reaches the settings stage and nothing else while every setting is at its default.

2.1.16._note: Captured from the hand-written Lua data stage before the Go port, re-verified against the Go data guest after it, and re-captured for 0.3.1, whose two startup cost settings are the only difference: the mod-settings dump moved from {} to those two prototypes and the data-raw dump did not move at all. Per engine and per mod set: the dump carries every prototype every mod defined. Only the DEFAULT settings are hashed; the variant and speed arms assert values.

base._stale: 0.3.3 pointed the legacy stub ITEM's place_result at the stub ENTITY rather than at bbb-balancer-part, which moves this arm's dump. Re-capture on a 2.1 binary: make mod && test/check-datastage.py --capture. The incumbent arm's DATA-RAW is not stale -- another mod owns balancer-part there, so the stub branch emits nothing and the item never existed to move. 0.3.3's recipe customizer moves this arm's MOD-SETTINGS dump and only that: `bbb-recipe-cost` gains the value `custom` and a composed `localised_description` listing every preset, and `bbb-recipe-ingredients` is a third setting (a string-setting with `auto_trim` and its own composed description). The data-raw dump does NOT move -- measured on Factorio 2.0.77, where both arms' normalised data-raw dumps are byte-identical either side of the change. Re-capture on a 2.1 binary: make mod && test/check-datastage.py --capture.

2.1.17._note: Captured on Factorio 2.1.17 (build 87315) at the 2.1.17 api pin, on the engine-bump round. EVERY FIELD IS 2.1.16'S TO THE DIGIT -- both mod sets' data-raw hash, the mod-settings hash and the prototype list checksum -- which is what a release carrying no prototype change looks like from this instrument, and matches `fklua api diff 2.1.16 2.1.17` reporting 0 breaking and 1 additive (RenderLayer gained a union arm, which is a runtime concept and reaches no prototype). It is recorded as its own line rather than aliased to 2.1.16's because a golden is PER ENGINE by construction: the equality is a measurement of this release, not a rule about the next one. Per engine and per mod set: the dump carries every prototype every mod defined. Only the DEFAULT settings are hashed; the variant and speed arms assert values.
